 A look ahead to the Nevada Wolf Pack football game against the Northern Illinois Huskies this Saturday at DeKalb, Ill.:
 KICKOFF : 12:30 p.m., Huskie Stadium (23,595 capacity).
 THE RECORDS : Nevada (3-6, 2-3); Northern Illinois (0-9, 0-5).
 THE SPREAD : Nevada is favored by seven points (total is 47.5).
 TV/STREAMING : Mountain West-Plus.
 RADIO : 105.7 FM.
 AT STAKE FOR NEVADA : The Wolf Pack needs to sweep its final three games this season to earn a bowl game invitation. Nevada has not been to a bowl game since 2021. A victory this weekend would also give Nevada its most victories (four) in a season since it was 8-5 in 2021.
 AT STAKE FOR NORTHERN ILLINOIS : The Huskies are looking to avoid their first winless season since 2020 when they finished 0-6 (season shortened by COVID-19). Northern Illinois has had just four winless seasons in its history. The first three: 0-6-1 in 1928; 0-8-1 in 1955; and 0-11 in 1997.
 THE COACHES : Jeff Choate (56 years old) is 9-25 overall, 4-16 in the Mountain West and in his third season at Nevada. Rob Harley (44 years old) is 0-9, 0-5 and in his first season as Northern Illinois' head coach. Harley was the Huskies’ defensive coordinator in 2025 after spending 2021-24 as Arkansas State defensive coordinator and 2015-20 as the linebacker coach at Pittsburgh. Harley, who is from Elmhurst, Ill. (a western suburb of Chicago), is a former safety at Ohio State (2001-05).
 THE RIVALRY : The Huskies and Wolf Pack split two games in 1993 and 1994 as members of the Big West. NIU won, 46-42, in Reno in 1993 while Nevada won, 35-31, in DeKalb in 1994.
 In the 1994 game, Nevada's Mike Maxwell passed for 328 yards and three touchdowns (the third was to Mike Senior from seven yards out with 2:09 to play) while Alex Van Dyke returned a kickoff 90 yards for a touchdown and caught a touchdown pass. NIU's Brian Grimes rushed for 157 yards in the 1994 game while Vaurice Patterson had 187 receiving yards in the 1993 meeting. The two schools were rivals in the Big West from 1993-95, but did not play in 1995. Nevada finished ahead of NIU in the Big West standings all three seasons.
 WHEN NEVADA HAS THE BALL : A.J. Bianco (51-of-102, 503 yards, two touchdowns, three interceptions) is listed as the starter at quarterback. Dominic Kelley (584 yards, five TDs) and Herschel Turner (520, 4) will run the ball while Damien Morgan (35-199-0), Gary Givens (20-308-1), Marshaun Brown (18-255-2) and Donnie Cheers (12-181-1) have been the favorite targets of the Nevada quarterbacks this season. The Wolf Pack is averaging 20.8 points a game.
 WHEN NORTHERN ILLINOIS HAS THE BALL : Quarterback Taron Dickens is 183-of-283 for 1,876 yards, nine TDs and seven interceptions. Dickens has run for 73 yards (one TD) on 72 carries. Telly Johnson (110-629-6) and Elijah Porter (66-312-2) lead the Huskies’ ground game. Dickens' top targets have been DeAree Rogers (70-719-5), La'Don Bryant (33-379-1), George Dimopoulos (21-259-1) and Cam Thompson (16-164-1). NIU is averaging 16.6 points a game, failing to score more than 24 points in any game.
 DICKENS' JOURNEY : NIU quarterback Taron Dickens spent the 2023-25 seasons at Western Carolina, an FCS school. Dickens had a highly productive season a year ago at Western Carolina, passing for 3,508 yards and 38 touchdowns with just two interceptions. At one point he completed 50 consecutive passes over two games (last four against Campbell and the first 46 against Wofford). He was 53-of-56 against Wofford. Dickens finished second in the Walter Payton Award (the FCS version of the Heisman Trophy) voting last season. Dickens, a Miami native, originally committed to North Carolina and head coach Bill Belichick after the 2025 season but ended up at Northern Illinois because of academic reasons, according to on3sports.
 NEVADA TURNOVER CONCERN : The Wolf Pack defense has not forced a turnover over its last five games (just three all season). The Wolf Pack offense has turned the ball over 17 times this year. Northern Illinois has forced 11 turnovers this year while turning the ball over 15 times.
 HUSKIES' SLOW STARTS : Northern Illinois has been outscored, on average, 33-13, over the first three quarters this season. They have lost by fewer than 10 points just twice this year, 28-24 at home to the FCS' Illinois State and 31-24 at UNLV. Five of their nine losses have been by 18-plus points.
 MORGAN PACK SAFETY VALVE : Wide receiver Damien Morgan leads Nevada with 35 catches but has picked up just 199 yards (no TDs). Morgan's average catch of 5.69 yards is the lowest by any Wolf Pack receiver (including wide receivers, tight ends and running backs) for those with 20 or more catches in a season since Nevada moved to the FBS in 1992. The only other player under six yards a catch with 20 or more catches in a season is running back Kelton Moore, who averaged 5.80 yards on 20 catches (116 yards) in 2018. Morgan, who spent the last three seasons at Idaho State, has had just five catches all season of 10 yards or more, two of which came against Middle Tennessee (26, 19 yards). His other 30 catches this year have averaged 3.86 yards.
 HUSKIES’ MOUNTAIN WEST DEBUT : The Huskies, who have lost 11 games in a row dating back to last season, are in their first year in the Mountain West after 29 seasons (1997-2025) in the Mid-American Conference, 17 as an independent (1966-74, 1986-92, 1996), three in the Big West (1993-95), and 11 more in the MAC (1975-85).
